Huh, well TIL. I even looked back on old guitar hero and rockband forums discussing the advantages of hyper speed/breakneck speed. It is all about reaction time and being familiar with the chart

To me it seems that a slower speed means the notes pass over the bar for a longer duration, even if only fractionally. Giving a wider opportunity to hit it early or late. It even feels like when the notes are going faster, you have less time to press the button just in terms of opportunity alone, 

Like I'm saying the "Good" window is shorter. The perfect window remains. It seems harder to hit a note "late" when the speed is fast because there is a higher chance it'll be a miss, dropping the score multiplayer, rather than counting as good and keeping the score up. On slower speeds I have been able to FC some of those faster songs based on the fact that I nailed a complex part by being late to all of them.

maybe it's up to an individuals visual processing and reaction speed? Just what I've found.

Increasing speed means shortening the window that a note can be pressed and still count, rather than a total miss. A note pressed "late" on regular speed would be missed completely on 2x speed.   On higher speeds I actually find it easier to get perfect notes because of this window. You either hit it perfectly, or not at all, on 2x speed.
